unit.label: Actions & plans
unit.title: What would you like to do?
unit.description: 13 new words and forms. Go, read, speak, and make a plan.

steps.prompt: Which phrase asks “where”, rather than pointing to “there”?
steps.explanation: 哪裡 (nǎlǐ) asks where. 那裡 (nàlǐ) points to there, and 這裡 means here.
來 is lái: come, with a rising second tone.

lessons.title: Read a book
lessons.subtitle: Actions, objects, and a word for and

steps.prompt: What does 和 join in 他和她都看書？
options: He and she: the two people.
steps.answer: He and she: the two people.
steps.explanation: 和 joins 他 and 她 into one subject. 都 follows that whole group, before 看書.
看 is kàn here. With 書, it means read: 看書.

lessons.title: Chinese and English
lessons.subtitle: Use a familiar character as a new word

steps.prompt: Which character means “writing; language in language names”?
steps.explanation: 文 (wén) means writing; language in language names.

steps.prompt: In 我學中文, what does 學 do?
options: It is the verb: learn or study.
It means student on its own.
steps.answer: It is the verb: learn or study.
steps.explanation: 學 is now the independent verb learn or study. 學生, with both characters, is the noun student.
文 is wén. It is the shared ending in 中文 and 英文.

lessons.title: Speak and listen
lessons.subtitle: Two actions for learning a language

steps.prompt: In a listening exercise, you play Chinese audio. Which phrase names listening to it?
steps.explanation: 聽中文 means listen to Chinese. 說中文 means speak Chinese. Listening does not by itself guarantee understanding.
說 is shuō: speak or say, with a level first tone.

lessons.title: What would you like to do?
lessons.subtitle: Wishes, intentions, and things you want

steps.prompt: Which sentence says you do not WANT to go?
steps.explanation: 不想 denies wanting. 我不去 says I do not go or I am not going, but does not explicitly say what I want.
想 is xiǎng: want to before an action, or think in other contexts.

lessons.title: I can speak English
lessons.subtitle: A learned skill, and an honest answer

steps.prompt: 你會說英文嗎？ You know how to speak English. Choose the short answer.
steps.explanation: This question asks about the skill with 會. Repeat 會 for yes, or 不會 for no.

steps.prompt: Which phrase specifically means “do not know HOW to speak Chinese”?
steps.explanation: 不會說 is about lacking the learned skill. 不想說 is not wanting to speak; 不說 simply negates speaking.
會 is huì. Here it expresses knowing how to do a learned skill.

lessons.title: Unit 4 review
lessons.subtitle: Where you go, what you do, what you want

steps.prompt: Choose the measure word in “I want this book”: 我要這 __ 書
steps.explanation: A new action does not change the book phrase: 這本書 still uses 本, just as it did in Unit 3.

newVocabulary.note: The destination follows the verb: 去那裡. The u in qù represents the ü vowel, written without dots after q.
Movement toward the speaker or the chosen reference point: 來這裡.
An information question word. Compare 那裡 (nàlǐ), there.
The object determines the English action: 看書 means read books.
Also pronounced hàn for and in Taiwan. Use it between people or things, not to join whole sentences.
A language name written with two characters; it counts as one word.
Shares 文 with 中文. It counts as one word, not two characters.
You know the character from 學生. Now practice it as an independent verb: 學中文.
Put the language directly after the verb: 說英文.
聽中文 names listening to Chinese; it does not by itself mean understanding it.
For want to, follow it with an action: 想學中文.
Can precede a thing you want or an action you intend to do.

newVocabulary.meaning: can; know how to (a learned skill)
newVocabulary.note: A learned ability here: 會說英文. Its negative is 不會 (bú huì).

去.note: 去 means go. Put the destination after it: 去那裡 = go there. Unlike 在 (be at), 去 describes movement.
去.memory: A 土-shaped top above a small, two-stroke lower shape.

parts.label: 土
parts.name: earth-shaped top
parts.description: The upper three strokes form 土, a shape you saw in 在. Recognize the shared shape without treating earth as a literal explanation of go.

parts.label: 厶
parts.name: two-stroke lower shape
parts.description: Write the angular turning stroke and then the dot. This 厶-shaped group helps distinguish 去 from other characters with 土.

來.note: 來 means come, toward the speaker or a place treated as the reference point. 來這裡 means come here. Learn 來 and 去 as a useful pair.
來.memory: A tall central shape with two smaller 人-like shapes tucked inside.

parts.label: 來
parts.name: overlapping whole shape
parts.description: The central 木-like strokes surround two small 人-like groups. Their strokes are interleaved, so follow the whole eight-stroke sequence rather than writing each visible part separately.

哪.note: 哪 appears in 哪裡 (nǎlǐ), meaning where. Notice the mouth component and third tone: 哪裡 asks where; 那裡 (nàlǐ) means there.
哪.memory: Add a small mouth to the left of the 那 you already know.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth
parts.description: 口 is the same three-stroke component as in 嗎. It is a useful visible clue for distinguishing 哪 from 那.

parts.label: 那
parts.name: 那 · nà
parts.description: 那 suggests the syllable na, but the tone changes: 那 is nà (that), while 哪 in 哪裡 is nǎ. The right side reuses all seven strokes of 那.

看.note: 看 covers several English actions, depending on what follows it. 看書 means read a book or read books. In these uses it is pronounced kàn.
看.memory: Imagine a hand shading an eye so it can look into the distance.

parts.label: 龵
parts.name: hand-shaped upper part
parts.description: The upper four strokes are a changed form of 手 (hand). The hand above the eye is a useful connection with looking.

parts.label: 目
parts.name: eye
parts.description: 目 means eye. Its five strokes form the lower block, connecting this character with seeing.

和.note: 和 joins people or things: 我和你 = I and you. We write hé in the pinyin; you may also hear hàn for this use in Taiwan. The meaning and word order stay the same.
和.memory: A grain-shaped left side beside a small mouth.

parts.label: 禾
parts.name: grain · hé
parts.description: 禾 is pronounced hé and helps with the hé reading of 和. The hàn reading used for and in Taiwan is a pronunciation to learn with the word, not from this sound clue.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth
parts.description: Recognize the three-stroke 口 shape on the right. It does not make grain plus mouth a literal meaning equation for and.

中.note: 中 can mean middle. In this unit it is the first character of 中文, Chinese. Learn the language name as a whole word, not as middle plus writing.
中.memory: A central vertical stroke passes through a small box.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: box shape
parts.description: The first three strokes make the box. Here it is a shape to recognize, not the word mouth in the meaning of 中文.

parts.label: 丨
parts.name: central vertical
parts.description: The final stroke passes down through the center and extends above and below the box.

文.note: 文 is connected with writing and language. It is the shared ending in 中文 (Chinese) and 英文 (English). Each language name counts as one word.
文.memory: A dot and horizontal at the top, then two long crossing strokes.

parts.label: 文
parts.name: one whole shape
parts.description: Learn the four strokes as one basic character. The lower crossing strokes should have room to spread; they are not two separate words.

英.note: 英 is the first character of 英文 (Yīngwén), English. This Taiwan stroke form has nine strokes, including four in the top component.
英.memory: A four-stroke plant component sits above a wider five-stroke lower shape.

parts.label: 艹
parts.name: plant component
parts.description: The top is the plant or grass component, written with four strokes in this Taiwan form. It reflects other uses of 英, not the meaning English.

parts.label: 央
parts.name: 央 · yāng
parts.description: 央 is a historical phonetic component. Modern yāng is only a rough clue to yīng, so learn the pronunciation with the whole word 英文.

說.note: 說 means speak or say. Put a language after it to say which language someone speaks. Keep the Traditional 言 component and the Taiwan 兌 shape on the right.
說.memory: The speech component you saw in 這 now stands on the left.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech
parts.description: 言 is associated with speech and language. Its seven strokes give a useful meaning connection in 說, speak or say.

parts.label: 兌
parts.name: 兌-shaped right side
parts.description: 兌 is a historical phonetic component, but its modern reading duì does not directly give shuō. Notice the two upper strokes, the small box, and the spreading legs.

聽.note: 聽 means listen or listen to. English needs to in listen to English; Mandarin can put the language directly after 聽. This longer character is worth learning slowly, one group at a time.
聽.memory: Find the ear on the upper left and the heart shape at the bottom right.

parts.label: left
parts.name: ear and lower left strokes
parts.description: The first six strokes form 耳 (ear), a clear connection with listening. Four more strokes finish the lower left group. Complete this whole side before moving right.

parts.label: right
parts.name: right-hand group with 心
parts.description: Work down through the upper marks and box-like shape, then the horizontal and the bottom 心 (heart) shape. These landmarks help memory; they are not a literal formula for how the character was created.

想.note: 想 can mean think. Before an action, it can express want to or would like to: 想看書 = want to read. The lesson will show where it goes in a sentence.
想.memory: A tree-and-eye shape sits above a heart.

parts.label: 相
parts.name: 相 · xiāng
parts.description: The upper nine strokes form 相, with 木 on the left and 目 on the right. Its reading xiāng points to the syllable xiang; 想 has a third tone instead.

parts.label: 心
parts.name: heart; mind
parts.description: 心 is connected with thoughts and feelings, a useful meaning clue for think or want. Keep its four strokes spread beneath the upper block.

要.note: 要 can name something you want or an action you intend to do. It often sounds more definite than 想. We will practice this wanting and intention use, not every meaning of 要.
要.memory: A wide upper block over the 女 shape you already know.

parts.label: 覀
parts.name: wide upper block
parts.description: The top six strokes form a 覀-shaped block. Notice its short inner verticals and wide base; the shape does not literally explain want.

parts.label: 女
parts.name: woman-shaped lower part
parts.description: Reuse 女 from 好 and 她, now underneath the upper block. Recognize the component without inventing a woman-related meaning for modern 要.

會.meaning: can; know how to (a learned skill)
會.note: 會 before an action can mean know how to do it. 我會說英文 means I can speak English. This is learned ability, not a general word for permission.
會.memory: A broad, roof-like upper group above a small lower block.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: upper nine-stroke group
parts.description: Start with the two spreading top strokes, then build the enclosed shapes below. Follow the guide carefully; the visible pieces do not give a simple meaning equation for can.

parts.label: 曰
parts.name: wide lower block
parts.description: The last four strokes form a wide 曰-shaped block. You saw a similar lower shape in 書. Keep it centered under the larger top.

u4-movement.title: Going somewhere, coming here
u4-movement.explanation: 去 means go, away from the speaker or the place treated as the reference point. 來 means come, toward that reference point. The destination follows the verb directly: 去那裡 (go there), 來這裡 (come here). You do not need an extra word for the English to.
u4-movement.remember: 在 gives a location: 我在這裡 (I am here). 來 and 去 describe movement. The verb stays the same for different people; do not add 是 before it.

u4-where.title: Ask where
u4-where.pattern: person + 在 / 去 + 哪裡？
u4-where.explanation: 哪裡 means where. Like 什麼, it stays in the position of the missing information. 你在這裡 (you are here) becomes 你在哪裡 (where are you). With 去, replace the destination instead: 你去哪裡 means where are you going.
u4-where.remember: Do not add 嗎 to this information question. Compare 哪裡 (nǎlǐ, where) and 那裡 (nàlǐ, there): a component and a tone make the difference. As in 你好, the first third tone of 哪裡 changes in speech; the pinyin keeps dictionary tones.

u4-actions.title: Say what someone does
u4-actions.explanation: An action verb can go directly after the person, followed by its object: 我看書 means I read books. 看 can mean look, watch, or read; with 書 it means read. There is no 是 before the action and no verb ending for he, she, or they. 書 without a number can refer to books generally.
u4-actions.remember: For an ordinary negative here, put 不 before the action: 不看. This does not mean did not read; past-event negatives come later. Add 嗎 for yes/no, or keep 什麼 in the object slot to ask what: 你看什麼？

u4-and.title: Join two people or things
u4-and.explanation: 和 means and when joining people or things. 他和她 means he and she. The combined phrase can be the subject; put 都 after the whole group to say both of them: 他和她都看書. The same joining pattern works with things, such as this book and that book.

examples.pinyin: tā hé tā dōu shì xuéshēng
examples.meaning: He and she are both students.

examples.pinyin: zhè běn shū hé nà běn shū

u4-and.remember: Use 和 to join nouns here, not as a general link between complete sentences or separate actions. We show hé in pinyin; hàn is also used for and in Taiwan.

u4-languages.title: Learn a language
u4-languages.explanation: 中文 means Chinese, and 英文 means English. In our lessons, speaking 中文 means speaking Mandarin. Both names end in 文. You already wrote 學 inside 學生; now use 學 as a word on its own: learn or study. Put the language after it: 我學中文.
u4-languages.remember: 中文 and 英文 are language names, not identities for people. No measure word is needed when saying which language you study. 學生 is one word, student; 學 is now a separate verb, learn or study.

u4-speech.title: Speaking and listening
u4-speech.explanation: 說 means speak or say; 聽 means listen or listen to. To name a language, put it directly after the verb: 說中文, 聽英文. English uses to in listen to English, but Mandarin does not add a separate word for it in this pattern.
u4-speech.remember: 聽 says that you listen; it does not by itself say that you understand. Keep the action + object order from 看書 and 學中文.

u4-wish.title: Say what you would like to do
u4-wish.explanation: Before an action, 想 can mean want to or would like to. It comes between the person and the action: 我想看書. There is no extra word for English to. You can use the same pattern with an action and a place, such as 想去那裡.
u4-wish.remember: Use 想 + an action for want to here. 想 has other meanings, including think about or miss; it is not a general replacement for want directly before a thing.

u4-intention.title: Want something, or intend to act
u4-intention.explanation: 要 can be followed by something you want: 我要這本書 (I want this book). It can also come before an action to express a more definite intention: 我要學中文 (I intend to study Chinese). 想 often sounds more like a wish; 要 often sounds more decided. Context still matters.
u4-intention.remember: Compare 想看書 (want to read) with 要這本書 (want this book). We are practicing desire and intention here; 要 is not an automatic translation of every English future tense.

u4-negative-wish.title: Say what you do not want
u4-negative-wish.pattern: person + 不 + 想 / 要 + rest
u4-negative-wish.explanation: To deny the wish itself, put 不 before 想 or 要. 我不想去 means I do not want to go. 我不要這本書 means I do not want this book. In 不想去, the negative belongs before want, not between want and go.

examples.meaning: I do not want to go.

examples.pinyin: wǒ bú yào zhè běn shū
examples.meaning: I do not want this book.

u4-negative-wish.remember: 不想 keeps bù before the third tone; 不要 sounds bú yào before the fourth tone. 不要 can also tell someone not to do something, but these examples are statements about what I want, not commands.

u4-ability.title: Say what you know how to do
u4-ability.explanation: Use 會 before an action for a learned skill: 我會說英文 means I know how to speak English. Put 不 before 會 for do not know how to: 我不會說中文. Add 嗎 to ask a yes/no question, and answer briefly with 會 or 不會.

examples.meaning: I do not know how to speak Chinese.

u4-ability.remember: 不說 means do not speak, 不想說 means do not want to speak, and 不會說 means do not know how to speak. This use of 會 is about skill, not permission. Its other uses, including predictions, come later.

u4-go-there.note: 我 + 去 + 那裡. The destination follows go directly, with no 是 or extra word for to.

u4-come-here.note: 來 points toward the speaker or the chosen reference point. Here the place is 這裡.

u4-where-going.note: Replace the destination after 去 with 哪裡. Do not move where to the front or add 嗎.

u4-where-book.note: 我的書 is the subject. 哪裡 fills the place slot after 在.

u4-read-book.note: 看 + a book means read. 這本書 still needs 本 because it points to this specific book.

u4-both-read.pinyin: tā hé tā dōu kàn shū
u4-both-read.meaning: He and she both read books.
u4-both-read.note: 他和她 is the whole group. 都 comes after that group and before 看.

u4-study-chinese.note: 學 is the action; 中文 is the language being studied. Do not add 是 before 學.

u4-study-both.note: 和 joins the two language names in the object slot. It is not joining two separate sentences.

u4-speak-english.note: 說 + 英文 = speak English. The verb stays the same regardless of who is speaking.

u4-listen-chinese.note: 聽 takes 中文 directly. Do not insert an extra word for the English to.

u4-all-speak.note: Reuse 他們 and 都, now before the action 說. 中文 names the language.

u4-want-read.note: 想 goes before the action 看書. It expresses a wish to read, not possession of a book.

u4-want-learn.note: 我 + 想 + 學 + 中文. 想 expresses the wish, 學 is the action, and 中文 is what you want to learn.

u4-want-book.note: 要 can go directly before a thing you want. Keep the full 這 + 本 + 書 phrase.

u4-plan-study.note: 要 comes before 學 to express a more definite intention in this example.

u4-want-go-where.meaning: Where do you want to go?
u4-want-go-where.note: Keep the order 你 + 想 + 去 + 哪裡. The question word still occupies the destination slot.

u4-dont-want-go.meaning: I do not want to go.
u4-dont-want-go.note: 不 goes before 想, because it is the wish that is being denied.

u4-can-english.note: 會 + 說 expresses knowing how to speak the language. It does not ask for permission.

u4-cant-chinese.meaning: I do not know how to speak Chinese.
u4-cant-chinese.note: 不 + 會 + 說 makes the skill negative. 不 sounds bú before the fourth tone of 會.

u4-can-question.note: Add 嗎 to the ability statement. Answer 會 (yes) or 不會 (no), not 有 or 沒有.
